correctness.rationale: Q=I+vv^T, v=e1+e2 in characteristic 2. For any symmetric binary zero-diagonal E with E1=0, v^T E^k v=0 for all k: odd powers by alternating quadratic form, even powers by vector parity and E1=0, k=0 by v^Tv=0. Matrix determinant lemma therefore gives chi(QE)=chi(E). With z^n-1=(z^m-1)^d, n=dm, m odd, the factor z+1 has multiplicity d and Rule90 acts as z^-1(z+1)^2 on its local algebra, yielding R zero Jordan blocks d/2,d/2. A=QR has ker dimension2 and ker(A^2) increment 1 when 4|n, else0, from parity sums of the swapped two-periodic kernel; fixed algebraic zero multiplicity d forces A blocks (d-1,1), including d=2. Kernel counts then give Fitting preperiod distributions for A (2^{n-d},3*2^{n-d}, then 2^{n-d+t} for 2<=t<=d-1) and R (2^{n-d},3*4^{t-1}*2^{n-d} for 1<=t<=d/2). Mean formulas follow summing finite geometric sums. Independently computed binary rank stabilization on all even n from 4 through 40, agreeing with both predicted nilpotent signatures; finite dimensions do not prove all-even n.

value.rationale: This natural partial-output permutation family was singled out as difficult for even ring sizes. A one-pair output swap leaves every spectral eigenvalue unchanged while almost doubling a power-of-two ring extinction horizon; the complete state preperiod census demonstrates a sharp Jordan-structure versus characteristic-spectrum distinction for finite GF2 dynamics.

final_claim: For every even binary Rule-90 cyclic ring n>=4, swapping only the first two output coordinates preserves the characteristic polynomial but changes nilpotent Jordan blocks from (d/2,d/2) to (d-1,1), d=2^v2(n); all preperiod counts and exact expectations follow, with worst-case extinction delay n-1 versus n/2 for powers of two.
